newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sends medical aid to Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: France sends medical aid to Palestinians.

text.p: France despatched 2.5 tonnes of medicine and medical equipment to the Palestinian autonomous territories on Friday as violent clashes between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians continued, officials said.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said Paris was seeking joint aid from the European Union, and the French embassy had also urged Israeli authorities to take steps to defuse tension.
The embassy had asked Israeli authorities to allow ambulances to drive to Makassed hospital in Jerusalem despite the closure of Palestinians territories.
France has asked Israel to close down the tunnel whose opening near Jerusalem's Temple Mount triggered the worst wave of violence since the 1993 Israel-PLO peace accords.
Israeli cabinet secretary Danny Naveh said police had closed the tunnel for security reasons and only temporarily.
French newspapers squarely blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for gun battles in which more than 50 died.
PLO representative in France Leila Shahid told RMC radio it would take a miracle and the intervention of major powers to prevent the threat of war returning to the whole Middle East.
She said that only full implementation of the Israeli-Palestinian peace accords could stop the violence.
"It needs a miracle and perhaps the intervention of the sponsors of the peace process, the United States, France, Europe to bring Netanyahu to reason," she said.
"Barring this, we are heading into a new war situation not only in Palestinian territories, but in the whole Middle East," she said.
The left-wing daily Liberation called on the West to step in, adding this would mean blaming Netanyahu for the deadlock and using coercion to make him resume the peace process.

"(U.S. President Bill) Clinton's sluggish call for bilateral appeasement does not really go in that direction. And without the Americans, the other Western powers' voice can hardly be heard," it said.

The conservative Le Figaro said: "It is high time for the candidate, whose words pass, to turn into a prime minister whose acts remain. Otherwise Benjamin Netanyahu will be seen as a dangerous amateur."
"Israel's demand for absolute security will remain unrealistic if the cost is total insecurity for Palestinians," it said.
Israel and the Palestinian Authority, blaming each other for the violence, were seeking a summit to try to salvage five years of U.S.-driven peacemaking.
